## Introduction and overview {#intro}

  ----------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Module                  Privacy and Uncertainty Quantification
  Code                    Not published — the module is announced in period 1 by the master's brochure; the 2026-2027 SynapseS course description has not been published (the S3/S4 tracks of the catalog are currently empty).
  Team and workload       Instructor, teaching hours and ECTS: not published · two complementary parts: **differential privacy** (mechanisms, composition, Rényi DP, DP-SGD, industrial deployments) and **uncertainty quantification** (calibration, deep ensembles, conformal prediction, LLM UQ) — the two families of guarantees that condition the responsible deployment of models.
  Period                  M2 · period 1 (announced)
  Status in the program   [M2]{.badge .m2}[Outside recommended track]{.badge .position} M2 program being finalized by the course instructors; the official description will not be communicated until the course description is published.
  ----------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Audience**: an engineer who must ship a model with guarantees on privacy and on calibration. **Empirical first**: the module starts from concrete failures — a classifier with 91% accuracy but an ECE of 0.18 (it is over-confident), a DP-SGD fine-tuning at ε = 2 that leaves the model unusable — and only then names the tools (mechanisms, composition, conformal prediction).

Differential privacy and uncertainty quantification are the two families of guarantees that a model needs before it can be deployed responsibly; the module treats them in two parts, privacy first (ch. 1–5), then uncertainty (ch. 6–12).

### What you will be able to do

-   State the definition of $\varepsilon$-differential privacy and prove that a mechanism satisfies it (Laplace, Gaussian, exponential);
-   Compose mechanisms (sequential and parallel theorems) and tighten the privacy budget with Rényi DP;
-   Choose between local and global DP, and explain precisely what DP-SGD modifies in SGD;
-   Read a reliability diagram and quantify the miscalibration of a classifier (ECE, Brier score);
-   Compare MC dropout and deep ensembles for estimating the uncertainty of a deep network;
-   Implement "split" conformal prediction and prove its marginal coverage guarantee;
-   Produce adaptive intervals via conformalized quantile regression;
-   Audit the uncertainty of an LLM and argue for a decision under uncertainty (alert threshold, abstention).

### Where this course fits in the program

M2 module offered in period 1, outside the recommended track: it is aimed at all students who want to add demonstrable guarantees to their profile, whatever their specialty.

**Prerequisites**: the limit theorems, confidence intervals and tests of [Refresher Statistics](../m1p1-refresher-statistics/index.html) (ch. 4 and 6), and the honest comparison of two models of [Machine Learning](../m1p1-machine-learning/index.html#model-comparison) (4.9). They are the language of the coverage guarantees of ch. 9. [Statistics in Action](../m1p2-statistics-in-action/index.html) (bootstrap, multiple testing) is optional, a reference for the same logic. The first encounter with differential privacy in ch. 5 of [Emerging ML](../m1p1-emerging-ml/index.html#ch5) helps if you took it; otherwise ch. 0–1 are self-contained.

**Downstream modules**: the privacy part of [Explainability, Security, Privacy of LLMs](../m2-explainability-security-privacy-llms/index.html) (memorization, membership inference, DP of LLMs, ch. 7–8) relies directly on the mechanisms and composition proved here. On the production side, the drift monitoring of [ML Ops and LLM Engineering Principles](../m2-mlops-llm-engineering/index.html#ch5) (ch. 5) tells when the data have moved; that module does not treat calibration or conformal prediction, and ch. 7–10 here say what to re-check when it fires (recalibration, a recomputed conformal quantile).

**Canonical home.** The DP proofs of ch. 1–4 (definition, post-processing, the Laplace mechanism, composition, Rényi DP, amplification by subsampling) are the reference derivations of these notes; the Gaussian mechanism, advanced composition and the subsampled-Gaussian accountant of DP-SGD are sketched or cited with their sources. [ESP of LLMs](../m2-explainability-security-privacy-llms/index.html#ch8) ch. 8, [Security & Robustness](../m2-security-robustness/index.html#ch8) ch. 7–8, [Advanced GNN](../m2-advanced-gnn/index.html#ch7) 7.4 and [Boosting → Tabular](../m2-boosting-foundation-tabular/index.html#ch8) ch. 8 use these results without re-proving them: this page is where the proofs are.

Ch. 5 is the short introduction to membership inference that those pages can cite; the full attack (shadow models, LiRA) is Security & Robustness Def. 8.3.

### Course outline

-   **Reminders: probability, concentration, DP as seen in M1** — puts the Markov/Hoeffding inequalities and the DP definition back in shape before going further.
-   **Differential privacy: the foundation** — definitions (neighboring, mechanism), the three structural properties (post-processing, group privacy, convexity) and sensitivity, the quantity that sets the noise of ch. 2.
-   **Mechanisms: Laplace, Gaussian, exponential** — sensitivity, noise calibration and the exponential mechanism for discrete responses.
-   **Composition: advanced and Rényi DP** — why naive compositions waste the budget, and how Rényi DP tightens it.
-   **Local versus global, and DP-SGD** — two trust models, then the algorithm that trains networks while preserving privacy.
-   **DP in industry and attacks** — real deployments, the $\varepsilon$ budget in practice, and attacks (reconstruction, inference) that motivate the theory.
-   **Uncertainty: sources and vocabulary** — aleatoric versus epistemic, and why modern networks are poorly calibrated.
-   **Calibration: diagrams, ECE, Brier** — measuring the gap between stated confidence and observed frequency.
-   **Bayesian deep learning: MC dropout versus ensembles** — two practical approximations of epistemic uncertainty, with their trade-offs.
-   **Conformal prediction: theorem and algorithm** — a distribution-free coverage guarantee in a few lines of code.
-   **Quantile and conformalized regression** — intervals whose width adapts to the query point.
-   **UQ for LLMs** — verbalized confidence, semantic coherence and the limits of the previous methods on generations.
-   **Applications: deciding under uncertainty** — assembling the tools to arbitrate abstention, alert and action in a real system.
-   **Exercises** — from proofs of mechanisms to conformal implementations on real data.
-   **Projects and assessment** — solo and group subjects, a written-exam proposal and a rubric.
-   **References** — the primary sources (Dwork, Rényi DP, Angelopoulos) to go to the text.

### Session plan {#sessions}

**24 h in class (assumed) = 8 sessions of 3 h.** The fiche publishes no teaching hours: 24 h is the M2 volume published for the Large Language Models course (CSC_53432_EP: 24 h, 2 ECTS) and is assumed here; the session split below is our proposal for covering these notes in that time. Level 1 = foundations (reviews, definitions, first worked examples), 2 = core methods, 3 = advanced material (recent research, open problems); the level never goes down from one session to the next.
